validity.researcher_notes:
EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: real and correctly classified. FGT's 'Phase V Expansion Project' is independently and repeatedly documented: FERC issued ONE certificate (Docket Nos. CP00-40-000, -001, -002) on July 27, 2001 authorizing the whole project (Federal Register FEIS notice, 66 FR ~2001-07-19, verified live at govinfo.gov: 'approximately 165.8 miles of pipeline loops and laterals,' '132,615 horsepower of additional compression at nine existing and three new compressor stations,' 'Mississippi, Alabama, and Florida,' cost '$452 million'). Two independent trade-press accounts of the COMPLETED project agree closely: Oil & Gas Journal ('166 miles of pipeline and 133,000 hp of compression,' '428 MMcfd of incremental firm gas transportation service') and IndustrialInfo.com ('167 miles of new pipeline,' 'adds 428 million cubic feet per day, bringing total system capacity to over 2.1 billion cubic feet daily,' '$452 million investment,' majority completed April 2002, construction in Mississippi/Alabama/Florida). Three independent origins (the regulator's own EIS notice, and two separately-bylined trade publications) agree Phase V as a WHOLE was ~166-168 miles / +428 MMcf/d / $452M -- built as one FERC-authorized project, not sub-certificated by 'stage.'

SPEC / DUPLICATE-ADJACENT FINDING (the reason for the caveat): GEM records this single project as THREE separate rows -- P4037 'Phase V Stages 1-2' (this row: 64 mi / 298 MMcf/d / $320M / start 2002), P4036 'Phase V Stage 3' (15 mi / 180 MMcf/d / $13M), and P4035 'Phase V Stage 4' (136 mi / 130 MMcf/d / $132M). Summed across all three: 215 miles / 608 MMcf/d / $465M -- respectively 29%, 42%, and 3% ABOVE every independently-verified total above. But the arithmetic is not random: P4037 (298 MMcf/d, $320M) + P4035 (130 MMcf/d, $132M) ALONE reproduce the independently-verified totals EXACTLY -- 298+130=428 MMcf/d (matches '428 MMcfd' / '428 million cubic feet per day' verbatim in both trade-press sources) and 320+132=$452M (matches '$452 million' verbatim in all three sources). Adding P4036 ('Stage 3': 180 MMcf/d, $13M) on top overshoots the true total by exactly P4036's own capacity and cost figures. This is strong circumstantial evidence that P4036 ('Stage 3') is either a duplicate/phantom entry or was double-counted, while THIS row's values (P4037, 298 MMcf/d / $320M) look like a genuine, correctly-allocated 2/3 share of the real project -- I just could not find any independent document that names 'Stages 1-2' specifically to confirm the 64-mile/298-MMcf/d split at that granularity (mileage alone does not reconcile as cleanly: P4037+P4035 = 200 mi vs. the ~166-168 mi independently reported, a ~33-34 mi gap even excluding P4036 -- so the length figures for these rows are not fully explained by this exercise). Per the aggregate-vs-segment rule, I did NOT cite any of these three system-level Phase V sources as a ref for this row's Length/Diameter/Capacity/Start/SegmentCost cells (none of them name 'Phase V Stages 1-2'); those cells are left UNRESOLVED with this note instead, per instructions ('note it and file a validity concern instead').

ORIGIN CONCERN: the gem.wiki page's own citation list has 'A Barrel Full' (abarrelfull.wikidot.com, cite_note-source1-1) as its single most heavily-used footnote (backlinks=32, i.e. attached to nearly every field on the page) -- and abarrelfull is a BANNED source under this project's standing rules. It is very likely the origin of GEM's 'Stages 1-2 / Stage 3 / Stage 4' subdivision and its specific numbers; I did not visit abarrelfull.wikidot.com (banned, per rule) so I cannot confirm this directly, but no independent source I found corroborates the stage-by-stage split, only the project-wide total.

ATTRIBUTION (owner) is covered in a separate validity object below. Of the 9 citations harvested from this row's wiki page, I opened/tested 3 directly (kindermorgan.com/pages/business/gas_pipelines/east/FGT/default.aspx -- now 404 dead; oilandgaswatch.org/pipeline/6491 -- returns a bare JS-app shell with no static data; fgttransfer.energytransfer.com/ipost/FGT/maps/system-map -- a JS map-viewer shell, no static data) and did not open the remaining 6 (eia.gov x2, fractracker.org, s3.amazonaws.com PGJ 'Planned Projects' PDF, texasenergyreport.com) due to this session's exhausted web-search budget; none of the 3 I opened yielded usable segment-level facts.
